sources.title: Treaty between the Holy See and Italy (Lateran Treaty)
sources.officialityEvidence: The official Vatican City State legislation site publishes the controlling treaty. Its public-access provisions preserve Holy See controls but do not enact Italian nationality-visa rules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The treasures of art and science ... will remain open to scholars and visitors.

sources.title: Visas: General Information
sources.publisher: Consulate General of Italy in Vancouver, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's official consular page specifically addresses travel to Vatican City and says its open border with neighbouring Schengen states makes travel without transit through Schengen practically impossible.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Vatican City microstates maintain open borders with neighbouring Schengen countries.

sources.title: Countries whose nationals are exempt from short-stay visas
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA maintains a current ordinary-passport short-stay schedule. It supports the Italian access leg, but its Nauru and Serbian-passport treatment conflicts with current EU-law material retained unresolved.
sources.supportingExcerpt: exempt from the visa requirement for stays of up to 90 days within a 180-day period

sources.title: Countries whose citizens need a visa to cross the border
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA publishes the current ordinary-passport countries subject to the Schengen visa obligation and expressly links the schedule to Regulation (EU) 2018/1806.
sources.supportingExcerpt: titolari di passaporto ordinario, sono soggetti o meno ad obbligo di visto Schengen

sources.title: Passports and equivalent travel documents
sources.publisher: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
sources.officialityEvidence: Italy's MFA states the current travel-document requirements for a visa and crossing the external border, including post-departure validity, issuance period and blank pages.
sources.supportingExcerpt: the residual period of validity ... shall be at least three months after the intended date of departure

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 30 December 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex marks this consolidated visa-list Regulation in force. Articles 3–4 and Annexes I–II govern the short-stay split and document-specific exceptions for the Italian access leg.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Nationals of third countries listed in Annex I shall be required to be in possession of a visa.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), consolidated 12 October 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: The current EUR-Lex consolidation defines persons enjoying free movement under Union law and its border-control annex expressly labels the EU, EEA and CH lane.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Persons enjoying the right of free movement under Union law.

sources.title: EU visa agreements with non-EU countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The Council's current official visa-agreements register states that the Nauru visa-free regime awaits conclusion of a waiver agreement; it conflicts with Italy MFA's live exemption schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Visa-free regime will apply only once Nauru and EU have concluded a visa waiver agreement.

sources.title: Directive 2004/38/EC: right of entry for Union citizens
sources.officialityEvidence: EUR-Lex publishes Article 5, requiring Member States to admit Union citizens with a valid identity card or passport without an entry visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No entry visa or equivalent formality may be imposed on Union citizens.

sources.title: European Travel Information and Authorisation System: current status
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The Commission's current Smart Borders page expressly states that ETIAS is not operating and no travel-authorisation applications are collected.
sources.supportingExcerpt: ETIAS is currently not in operation and no applications for travel authorisations are collected.

sources.title: Law No. CXXXI on citizenship, residence and access, 22 February 2011
sources.officialityEvidence: The official Vatican City State PDF is the text of Law CXXXI. Article 1 directly identifies citizens of the State and regulates acquisition of citizenship.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Sono cittadini dello Stato della Città del Vaticano.

sources.title: Vatican City State ordinary passport, first issued 18 December 2025
sources.officialityEvidence: The Vatican City State ePassport service publishes the current ordinary VA passport specification and issue date.

sources.title: Population
sources.officialityEvidence: The Vatican City State's current population page identifies Vatican citizens and says citizenship, residence permits and access formalities are governed by specific provisions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Acquiring and losing citizenship ... and any other formality related to access are regulated by specific provisions.

policies.title: Vatican ordinary passport: citizenship
policies.summary: A traveller presenting the current Vatican City State ordinary passport is classified as citizenship rather than as a foreign visitor-visa relationship.
conditions: Law CXXXI directly identifies citizens of the Vatican City State, and the State directly publishes its current ordinary VA passport. This is a narrow catalogue citizenship classification, not a claim that citizenship automatically grants public access to every controlled Vatican area.

Citizenship, residence and access are governed by Vatican-specific provisions. Dual nationality, residence, work, diplomatic, service, temporary-service and special-document treatment is outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: EU ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: For a short public visit, these travellers need no entry visa for the controlling Italian/Schengen access leg; this route finding does not say that a Vatican instrument imports Italian rules.
conditions: Vatican City is an enclave with an open border adjoining Italy. This records the necessary Italian/Schengen route, not Vatican membership of Schengen or an adoption of Italian law by Vatican City.
A Union citizen needs a valid identity card or passport for Italian entry; no Italian entry visa or equivalent formality applies.

The Lateran Treaty normally leaves St Peter's Square open to the public and reserves public-access regulation to the Holy See. No ordinary public-visitor maximum duration is established by the directly reviewed Vatican sources.
No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date.

policies.title: EEA and Swiss ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: For a short public visit, these EEA and Swiss travellers use the visa-free Italian/Schengen access leg; this is a route finding, not a claim that Vatican City imports Schengen law.
conditions: The current Schengen Borders Code directly recognises persons exercising free movement under Union law and distinguishes the EU, EEA and CH border lane. This policy records the necessary Italy/Schengen route only.
Vatican City is not a Schengen member. The Lateran Treaty preserves Holy See control of Vatican public access and does not itself enact Italian nationality-visa rules.
No ordinary public-visitor maximum duration is established by the directly reviewed Vatican sources. No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources.
ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date. Residence, family-member, diplomatic, service and special-document rules are outside this ordinary-passport baseline.

policies.title: Visa-exempt Schengen-access ordinary passports: visa-free visitor access
policies.summary: With the required qualifying document, these visitors are exempt from the Italian/Schengen short-stay visa needed to reach Vatican City; this route finding does not establish a separate Vatican visitor visa.
conditions: The controlled Italian/Schengen short-stay allowance is up to 90 days in any 180-day period; it is not evidence of a separate Vatican visitor-stay maximum.
Biometric ICAO-compliant passports are required for AL, BA, GE, MK, MD, ME, UA and XK. Taiwan requires an identity-card number; HK and MO require the respective named SAR passport.

A valid travel document and the ordinary Italian external-entry conditions remain required. Residence-permit, family-member, refugee/stateless, diplomatic/official/service, minor and other document-specific rules are not flattened into this nationality baseline.
No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date.

policies.title: Schengen-visa-required ordinary passports: visitor access via Italy
policies.summary: These ordinary passports need the advance Italian/Schengen visa required for the access route through Italy; the route finding neither calls it a Vatican visa nor says Vatican law imports Italian rules.
conditions: This is the advance Italian/Schengen visa for the access route through Italy, not a Vatican visa. Vatican public access remains subject to Holy See controls.
For the Italian access leg, the ordinary travel document must normally remain valid three months after planned Schengen departure, have been issued within ten years and have two free pages.

The Schengen short-stay limit is up to 90 days in any 180-day period. It does not establish a Vatican local visitor-stay maximum; no such ordinary visitor duration was found in the reviewed direct Vatican material.

No separate Vatican eVisa, ETA or visa-on-arrival route was established by the reviewed sources. ETIAS is not operating for the Italy/Schengen access leg on the research date. Residence, family-member, minor, diplomatic/official/service, refugee/stateless and other special-document exceptions remain outside this ordinary-passport nationality baseline.

unresolved.reason: The binding current EU Annex II treatment for qualifying Serbian biometric passports conflicts with current Italian MFA guidance on Serbian passport qualification. The reviewed Vatican material establishes the Italy/Schengen route but does not resolve that access-leg conflict, so no ordinary-passport baseline is assigned.

Italy MFA's live exemption schedule names Nauru, while the current Council register says the EU–Nauru visa-free regime applies only once a waiver agreement is concluded. The reviewed Vatican material does not choose between those official access-leg sources, so no ordinary-passport baseline is assigned.
